title: Getting to Know You: Data Reveal
topic: Statistical questions, sample vs. population, confounding variables

items.prompt: The class collected data from 12 of the 42 students in the class. This group of 12 students is called a:
items.rationale: A sample is a smaller group selected from the larger population.

items.prompt: The full group of 42 students in the class is called the:
items.rationale: The population is the entire group being studied.

items.prompt: Suppose students who sit in the front row both wear glasses more often AND raise their hands more often. Seat location could be a confounding variable because:

choices.A: It has nothing to do with either behavior
choices.B: It might influence both variables, making them appear connected when they aren't directly related
choices.D: Confounding variables never affect real data

items.rationale: A confounding variable is a hidden factor that can affect two other variables, creating a misleading relationship.

items.prompt: Which of these is a statistical question?

choices.B: How old are the students in my class?

items.rationale: A statistical question anticipates variability in the data collected to answer it (different students have different ages).

items.prompt: If 12 out of 42 students were surveyed, what percent of the class was surveyed? Round to the nearest whole percent.
